verses.1: Brothers, don’t have faith in our Lord Jesus Christ without being sincere in your actions.
verses.2: For if a man with golden bracelets enters your assembly, it will be because he is rich in appearance. But even a poor man who is shabbily dressed can also enter your assembly.
verses.3: Then look at the beggar with your bright eyes, and say, “Sit here properly.” And to the beggar, say, “Sit there under my roof.”
verses.4: Didn’t you also judge yourselves, and became the subjects of evil people’s discussions?
verses.5: Hear me, my beloved brothers. Did not God choose those who are poor in this world as heirs to the kingdom he promised to those who love him?
verses.6: But you honored the poor. It’s not that the rich people are not worthy of your respect. They themselves also try to bring you before judges.
verses.7: Don’t they slander the good name that has been given to you?
verses.8: But if you are to enforce the royal law according to the written laws, then do so well. Treat your neighbor as yourself.
verses.9: But if you try to deceive others, then you are committing a sin. You are violating the law by doing so.
verses.10: For if everyone obeys the law, then in one person, everyone becomes liable.
verses.11: For he said, “Do not commit adultery.” He also said, “Do not kill.” But if you do not commit adultery, then you are a law-breaker.
verses.12: Thus must you speak, and thus must you act, in order to be judged as being free according to the law of freedom.
verses.13: For judgment is a form of injustice when it fails to practice kindness; kindness, on the other hand, is recognized through judgment.
verses.14: What use, brothers, is it if someone claims to have works, when in reality he doesn’t? Can faith really possess those works? It cannot.
verses.15: If there are brothers or sisters who are naked and have no means of support,
verses.16: Let someone from among you speak to them. Let them live in peace, be nourished and filled, but do not give them what is necessary for their bodies. What’s the point of that?
verses.17: Similarly, faith, if it has no actions, is dead in itself.
verses.18: But someone else says: “You have faith, and I have works. Show me your faith apart from your works. And I will show you my faith through my works.”
verses.19: Do you really believe that there is a God? You’re right. Even the demons believe in Him and worship Him.
verses.20: Do you want to know, oh man who is empty, that faith is slow in comparison to actions?
verses.21: Abram, our father, was not worthy of being honored for his actions. He did not bring his son Isaac onto the altar as an offering.
verses.22: You see that faith completes the works of God. And from those works, the faith is fulfilled.
verses.23: And the prophecy was fulfilled. Abraham believed in God, and he was justified before Him. He became a friend of God.
verses.24: You see that a person is worthy of praise because of his actions, not just because of his faith.
verses.25: Similarly, too, the prostitute Raab was not rewarded for her actions. She was deceived by the messengers, and she was sent away on another path.
verses.26: For just as the body is dead apart from the spirit, so too is faith dead apart from its actions.
